note: FINAL SETTLED ACCOUNT of the worktree-freshness thread -- supersedes e7c5bcb8, 5fd03dec and 9370de8a. Four passes, two readers, one 150-line script. TWO REAL DEFECTS. (1) scripts/worktree-take.sh lines 43-46 early-exit on an existing DEST before the invalidation step, so the freshness warnings FIRST suggested fix does nothing for the only tree that can print it. The sentence at line 149 offers a SECOND fix -- force a rebuild of the affected crates -- and that one is sound, so the hazard is the asymmetry: a reader taking the dead clause does nothing and believes they acted. (2) NEW, found by the lefford queue session and MEASURED here: line 135 is echo hits pipe sed pipe head -10, under this files set -euo pipefail at line 38. Once head has taken ten lines it exits; if sed still has data to write it takes SIGPIPE and returns 141; pipefail propagates it and set -e kills the script BEFORE the explanation paragraph and the fix line ever print. Remediation becomes unreachable exactly when contamination is worst. It also exits 141 rather than 1, so a caller reading exit codes sees a signal death, not a check failure -- worktree-take.sh:224 swallows both under || true, so a human at a shell is who gets the bare 141. MEASURED THRESHOLD, on the identical construct: 359 paths at about 42 KB exits 0 and the next line runs; 700 paths at about 83 KB exits 141 and it does not; 1500 likewise. Consistent with a 64 KiB pipe buffer. Fix is one character of plumbing -- sed 10q, or brace head -10 semicolon cat to devnull -- not a redesign. IT DID NOT FIRE IN MY CASE, AND THE REASON IS A NUMBER I GOT WRONG AND PUBLISHED THREE TIMES. I reported 756 contaminated files as the scripts finding. It is not. 756 is MY grep -rl over every file recursively under deps, including the rlib, rmeta and .d entries the script DELIBERATELY excludes -- its own comment says those are most of the 24,544 entries and are not what a test runs. By the scripts actual criterion (find -maxdepth 1 -type f -perm u+x) the count is 359 plus 1 plus 1 = 361, about 42 KB, UNDER the threshold. My run printed the full trailer and exited 1; verified by re-running it just now. So the peer estimated I had crossed the threshold using MY misattributed figure, and had I not measured, we would have jointly CONFIRMED a defect that did not occur -- the right measurement attributed to the wrong instrument, propagating into a second sessions reasoning and nearly producing a false positive. THE COUNT IS NOW THE FINDING: four defects and two wrong corrections in 150 lines, across two readers who each stopped early in a different place -- twenty lines above the header, mid-sentence, and at the boundary of a pipeline. Every one was reachable by reading the file; none by reading the function. And the shape recurs at every level: head -10 displays a set smaller than it received, and under pipefail destroys the process that would have explained the difference; my grep counted a set larger than the tool counts and I attributed it to the tool.
